item.title: Why Pearl-Cohn's return to TSSAA football state championship was never in doubt
item.description: LEXINGTON — The thought crossed Marshall commit Lance Donaldson' s mind that his Pearl-Cohn football career could be over. With two weeks left in the regular season, the Firebirds' leading rusher suffered an ankle injury against White House on Oct. 23 , forcing him to miss the final week of the regular season and potentially more. He said the injury was "a blessing in disguise," letting him add an extra element to his game and be a better player for his team. Donaldson logged 54 yards and two touchdowns on 13 carries giving Pearl-Cohn an edge in a 42-16 victory against Lexington (13-1) in TSSAA football playoff semifinals , in Class 4A on Nov. 27. More TSSAA football championship game pairings for 2026 BlueCross Bowl matchups The win pushes Pearl-Cohn (11-3) back into the 4A state championship game where it will face Alcoa (14-0) at 10 a.m. CT on Dec. 5 at Finley Stadium in Chattanooga. Its the second straight trip to the BlueCross Bowl for Pearl-Cohn and the program's eighth overall championship appearance, having won titles in 1996, 1997 and 2023. "He's (Donaldson) been playing lights out on both sides of the ball," said Pearl-Cohn coach Tony Brunetti, who will coach in his sixth title game on Dec. 5. "That's why he's such a powerful kid and is signing with Marshall next week." Part of Donaldson's deep dive into his game was getting to know those around him. He wanted to get closer to his linemen, not just as teammates, but really understanding the details of what they were doing in front of him. "I feel like my game has gotten better (since the injury)," Donaldson said. "I was able to look at my game from a mental standpoint and look at the things I could do better. Now, I'm able to attack those points and strengthen the ones I'm already good at. Since returning from injury, Donaldson has contributed six touchdowns in four games. Prior to that, he had just four scores in nine games. "He (Donaldson) does everything the right way," Brunetti said. "You don't see him talking or anything. He's a hard-nosed player. He's even lifting weights before the game. Donaldson is hoping for a full-circle moment against Alcoa in Chattanooga . Like many Pearl-Cohn seniors, his career started off with a state championship in 2023 . He wants to leave the same way he came in. His Firebirds took care of business, handing Lexington (13-1) its only loss this season. It'll be a tall task for Pearl-Cohn as Alcoa has won 11 consecutive state titles. "It's great to get one coming in and to get another going out is going to be an amazing feeling," Donaldson said. item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 26: Timur Tutierov of Sunderland scores his team’s first goal during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Sunderland AFC and Jagiellonia Bialystok at Stadium of Light on November 26, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) | Getty Images The searchlight casting its beam into the cold winter’s night, the fireworks, the anthem, the opposition from a far-flung corner of the continent – European football on Wearside, how incredible is that? Yes, I remain excited and enthralled by the whole experience. I think this new format for the three competitions is very cleverly designed; it maintains interest, and the idealist in me is glad that there is such a breadth of clubs and communities coming together, united in football. And then reality hits – or does it? What exactly is that reality? It is very easy to criticise the manager and the players when things don’t go the way we hoped for. Yet these are essentially the same people who got us into this incredible position in the first place. We do need to try to keep a sense of perspective on all of this, not get sucked into some reactionary doom spiral and work out positive ways forward. Let’s consider some of the feelings and concerns that are at the forefront of Sunderland supporters’ minds. When Régis Le Bris was appointed, there seemed to be a coming together of like-minded people at the helm of the club, and there was talk of a long-term plan and “the project”. In my time as a Sunderland supporter, that is pretty revolutionary talk, yet eminently sensible. Over my lifetime, North-East football has been beset by short-termism, constant changes of manager and boardroom personnel, perhaps with the exception (to a degree) of Middlesbrough and Steve Gibson. The plan was clearly for Sunderland to return to the top table and establish themselves in the Premier League. That return probably happened sooner than expected, and what followed last season definitely went way beyond expectations. So the club is possibly still playing catch-up, trying to cope with the significant extra demands at an earlier stage than they hoped for. Recruitment did not go as planned over the summer, and injuries to key players have compounded problems, yet it is important to stick to financial probity and keep working to build a sustainable football club. The players I watch on the pitch are good enough to stay in this league as long as they commit to the cause as they did against Chelsea and Villa. item.title: Sunderland’s Defensive Fragility: Why Are We Making So Many Mistakes?
item.description: Sunderland of 2025/26 was a stubborn unit and one which was an absolute pain in the arse to play against. More importantly, we were a tight defensive unit which defended en masse and backed ourselves against any forwards in the league. The most important thing of all was that we didn’t make many individual mistakes at all. This season, although the back-to-back clean sheets against Chelsea and Villa are an improvement, it feels as though every single goal we concede comes from an error from one of our players who looked so strong last year. The latest in this was Reinildo’s mistake, leading to Jagiellonia Białystok being gifted their equaliser on Thursday night. It was the latest in a series of worrying, schoolboy errors; the Coventry game was full of them, as was the trip to Bournemouth – take your pick. There haven’t been many goals we’ve conceded this year where the opposition have taken us apart. It doesn’t feel like we’re getting outplayed; it feels like we are just letting opponents dominate the ball and giving them chance after chance to keep on. The issue is that we sit back and have this obsession with passing the ball backwards, and on too many occasions we invite pressure onto ourselves. When confidence is rock bottom, this is asking for trouble, and this constant need to pass back and turn down chances to drive forward with the ball – which was successful last season – is proving to be a recipe for disaster. Defenders don’t look comfortable on the ball, and too many of our forwards don’t seem keen to be on the ball on the few occasions we get it to them. All of this combines to make for a team that, in terms of confidence, is a shell of what it was last year. The frustration is that we have a lot of senior defenders who have combined hundreds of appearances under their belts. Reinildo and Omar Alderete have almost 600 appearances between them; they are two of the players who made us so successful defensively last season. Yet this season, they’ve looked like completely different players, although I’ll say Alderete has struggled a lot more than Reinildo, and his early exit on Thursday after a ropey performance sums up his season. We are missing the spine of our team; this goes without saying. Dan Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey are three key figures any club would miss. Having them back sooner rather than later will make a huge difference to our fortunes. item.title: Sunderland’s European Frustration: This Simply Isn’t Good Enough
item.description: I should prefix this by saying it refers to the Europa League only. The Premier League is different, but has its own set of issues. Two problems persist at Sunderland right now. One was quite predictable, but the other gets the blood pressure up to dangerous levels. We are told with regularity that the Premier League takes priority. Now, I don’t know about anyone else, but when I thought of the prospect of playing Europe’s leading lights (no offence to Jagiellonia, but that didn’t include them), I quite honestly thought the Premier League campaign could go and stick its head up a dead bear’s bum. In fairness, that was me forgetting to factor in the chance we might spend a large part of the group stage in the relegation zone. Clearly, that has affected priorities. And I understand that, to an extent. By God, was it evident on Thursday night that the side selected would largely rather not have been there. It was a timid performance that wouldn’t have looked out of place in League One. To emphasise the point, the opposition striker (loosely put) scored one goal in 24 Championship appearances for Oxford last season. He was, by way of review from an Oxford-supporting pal of mine, “shite.” And yet, despite the limitations of our opponent, there was so much phoning it in, you’d think our lads were part of a live telethon to raise funds for a new attacking coach. Which brings me to the big question: what the hell are we doing in training all week, so that the end result is an utter lack of thrust, threat and attacking invention? Why is it that there are no partnerships across the pitch? The players should be far more connected than they are, but they look inert; coached to the point that they have no idea what to do, apart from admiring the opposition in front of us. Or perhaps undercoached, producing a similar effect. Yes, Jagiellonia had lovely shirts, but lads, there’s a football match to be played here. We haven’t all turned up at the game because we want to get away from our families, or because we like sitting in traffic on Wessington Way. It’s because we want to see our club in a competition we’ve dreamed of for years, if not decades. And now it’s here, I’m watching some of the lads play like a dropped PlayStation controller. item.title: OTD (28/11/1998): Gavin McCann Makes His Debut For Sunderland
item.description: Gavin Peter McCann was brought to the club by Peter Reid in 1998 from his old club Everton, for £500,000 – in what turned out to be a very decent piece of business, dropping down a division in the hope of more game time. Arriving in the 1998/99 Division One-winning season (that fantastic 105-point haul), he initially had limited opportunities in what was a very successful Sunderland side. He made his debut, coming on as a substitute, against Sheffield United at Bramall Lane, in a superb 4-0 away victory. But he only really started to settle in his first full season at the club in the FA Carling Premiership, initially in the number 11 shirt (when numbered shirts still meant something!). He was a well-built, strong player, standing just shy of 6ft. Once in the team, he started to become a standout player at the Stadium of Light, with fantastic balance, a great insight and a range of passing ability. He was a strong presence on the pitch, a great tackler, with the ability to get from box to box. Looking back now, in my mind’s eye, for me he resembles the style of a Ray Kennedy (for Liverpool) or a poor man’s Kevin Ball. He got his first full game that December, in a 2-0 home win against Crystal Palace, and in that season’s League Cup semi-final, first leg against Leicester City, he scored his first-ever professional goal, pulling a goal back after we’d gone behind 2-0. We lost 3-2 on aggregate that year. In our memorable campaign back in the Premier League (the first of two seventh-placed finishes), Gavin played 26 times, scoring four and assisting three. There was no hint of second-season syndrome, and McCann was again an integral part of Reid’s team in the 2000/2001 season, getting his first of three goals with a late strike against Arsenal. For me, one of Gavin’s best goals in a Sunderland shirt. The terrier that was Alex Rae robbed Patrick Vieira on the edge of the box, and McCann didn’t hesitate to sweep the ball across the keeper into the far corner of the net to earn a late equaliser. His consistent, powerful performances gained him a call-up to the England squad in February 2001. He came on in the second half in a 3-0 friendly victory against Spain. It was, unfortunately, his only cap. We struggled the following season, and Gavin didn’t register a goal or an assist, but he did play in 29 league matches, the most he’d played in a season for Sunderland. He surpassed that the following season by one match, as we sleepwalked into relegation. Too good for second-tier football, he left for Aston Villa in a £2.25 million deal in July 2003 – a decent-sized profit from when we’d bought him. He spent four seasons at Villa Park before joining Bolton Wanderers in July 2007 for £1 million. He did play in the UEFA Cup whilst there, but sadly had to retire in 2010 due to injury. item.description: I don’t know where the Kentucky Wildcats go from here. They just lost at home to an unranked Wichita State team in overtime, and that may not even have been the worst part. The Cats led by 14 in the first half and lost 73-71 in overtime. At home. On the 50th Anniversary of Rupp Arena’s opening. Kentucky is now 4-3 going into December. Four and three, a far cry from the standard this program once held. Kentucky got out-rebounded 55-36 at home and 23-12 on the offensive glass. That’s unacceptable for any program claiming to be NCAA Tournament-caliber. MVP: Rupp Arena, Big Blue Nation Give the fans credit. A lot of credit. Black Friday night. 9:00 tip. They showed up, trying to will the Cats across the finish line. Against Wichita State. This wasn’t Duke or North Carolina or Louisville or Tennessee. It was Wichita State. Big Blue Nation showed up and were imploring the Cats to finish down the stretch. These fans deserve better. Box Score First Half It was a spirited start for Kentucky Friday night. Even though they only scored four points in the first four-plus minutes, there was intensity and energy on the floor and on the team bench. Franck Kepnang, getting the start for an injured Malachi Moreno, scored the first four points for the Cats, including two on an alley-oop dunk. Kepnang also had an emphatic block just before the media timeout, practically spiking the ball out of bounds. But the Cats’ offensive struggles would continue for the next few minutes. In fact, the Cats went over five minutes without scoring, until Alex Wilkins nailed a three-pointer to cut the deficit to 8-7. item.description: Texas Longhorns defensive lineman Alex January (97) dives after Texas A&M Aggies wide receiver Mario Craver (1) in the first quarter of the Lone Star Showdown game between Texas and Texas A&M at Kyle Field in College Station, Nov. 27, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) COLLEGE STATION - Georgia isn't quaking in its boots after this one but the Texas Longhorns earned a chance to play their nemesis in what will be an historic showdown for the SEC championship. No one said it this would be easy. OK, I did since had the Longhorns taking down the reeling Texas A&M Aggies by a 31-17 score. Not the first time I've misfired, but the result was what many of us predicted would happen; at least if we're talking about the old moneyline. At this point of the season, the only result that matter is the one that places your team under the "W" or the "L" in the ledger. Texas' 16-6 win came before 109,570 at Kyle Field, including Aggies fans who showed up for meeting No. 121 and an end the most-lost season in many a year. And it was about as ugly as the scored indicated. The Texas offense struggled like it did at LSU. Quarterback Arch Manning locked in on receivers and threw an interception in the end zone that cost the Horns a chance to go up double digits with 11 minutes, 4 seconds remaining, but the defense rode in to save the day, like it has on so many occasions. To his credit, Manning (on an 18-for-34, 143-yard passing night that had mall walkers everywhere appreciating the pedestrian showing) helped clinch the win with a 7-yard scramble that set up Gianni Spetic's 42-yard field goal, putting the Horns comfortably in front. UT finished the regular season at 10-2 - that's a preseason prediction I nailed - but the offensive output we witnessed won't cut in the SEC title game against the two-time defending conference champs. The good news is Steve Sarkisian and his staff have plenty of time to come up with a good game plan for the Dec. 5 matchup in Atlanta. item.description: Coming out of a decade of dominance by Manchester City is a new experience in itself With just one win in their past seven matches in all competitions, Manchester City enter this Sunday’s Premier League clash with Arsenal in desperate need of a win. Forgetting the state of the Premier League table, Enzo Maresca’s side needs a win for their confidence. Across the past seven games, City have looked every bit a team in transition. Which is exactly what they are. After a decade of watching City play with ruthless efficiency under Pep Guardiola, it is a new experience in itself to watch this City team struggle to find their feet. But for Enzo Maresca’s side it is a necessary step to take on their journey and development. It is time to adjust expectations on this Manchester City to what the reality of their situation is. Barring the final two seasons of Pep Guardiola’s reign as Manchester City manager, the expectation was that his team was one of the favourites for every competition they entered. This changed over the 2024-25 & 2025-26 seasons. Manchester City began a rebuild of their squad that had conquered every conceivable mountain in their path. After a trophy-laden era, City have continued on the path of rebuilding their squad with an eye on constructing their next era of success. The biggest step in that process was the appointment of Enzo Maresca as Pep Guardiola’s successor. Enzo Maresca had a dream start to life as City manager. His team won eight consecutive matches in all competitions to begin the season. A 4-2 defeat to PSG ended that run. From that point onwards, Enzo Maresca’s side has appeared disjointed and lool every bit a team adapting to their new managers demands, tactics and expectations. It has been a jolt to the system to see a City side at sixes and seven’s all over the pitch. But it isn’t a surprise to see it take place. Speaking yesterday ahead of Manchester City’s massive Premier League fixture against Arsenal, Enzo Maresca said he is remaining calm during his team’s poor run of form. Also, Maresca said that patience is needed for his team to come together. He explained: “ Transition requires time. When we won seven games, people probably thought here at City there is no transition. But I said many times I am not a magician, there is transition. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BUFFALO, N.Y. — Go figure. The Pittsburgh Penguins won, and did so with the youth movement leading the way, while a few of the roughest performances were submitted by the most established veterans. The game wasn’t always pretty or even well played. To the Penguins’ credit, they overcame a sloppy and sleepy start and played increasingly well, submitting their best in the third period when it mattered most to beat the Buffalo Sabres 6-3 at KeyBank Arena. The primary and perhaps ONLY takeaway is that the game was a showcase for the youngsters fighting to crack the lineup on a regular basis, and it was certainly not a game to remember for the Penguins’ elder members. Rutger McGroaty, Ville Koivunen , and Ben Kindel each had one goal and one assist. Kris Letang and Blake Lizotte scored the other goals. Evgeni Malkin added his second point with an empty-net goal. Kindel, 19, was quite good and had good jump. He was probably the team’s best player, and that’s a foray into the real story of Friday’s win, which transcends the score. The story of the game was not simply the Penguins gradually improving the quality of team play but specifically, it was those born in the 21st century who were the players to do it. Unmistakably, the first period was achingly bland and uncompetitive for both teams. Perhaps it was a turkey coma for both teams, but anyone who missed the first period could consider themselves lucky, though the teams were tied 2-2. The second period has been the tiger trap for the Penguins, but instead of destroying their chances in the middle 20 minutes, the Penguins gained a bit of an edge, and they increasingly controlled the game, starting with goals from Rutger McGroarty and Ville Koivunen. That momentum continued, and in the third period, the Penguins outshot Buffalo 9-6, outchanced them 8-4, and allowed…zero goals. item.title: Jesper Wallstedt Wants to Play Goal in 70 Games Per Year for Wild
item.description: Jesper Wallstedt Wild Getty Minnesota Wild goalie Jesper Wallstedt says that he wants to play goalie in more than 70 games for his team going forward. Wallstedt has been incredible for Minnesota this season, helping the team to the best record in the Western Conference while putting up outstanding individual numbers for the Wild. With Filip Gustavsson finally back from his offseason hip surgery, Wallstedt is expected to get more rest for Minnesota after starting most of the team’s games in the first two months of the season. But if it were up to him, he would start in over 70 games per season. Jesper Wallstedt Wants to Shoulder Heavy Load for Wild Speaking to Joe Smith of The Athletic , Wallstedt would like to follow in the footsteps of his idol, New York Rangers legend Henrik Lundqvist, who played goal in 70+ games for four straight seasons for NY. “Honestly, I think so. If you want your goalie to play, he can play. I’ve seen this narrative of a lot of media saying that goalies burn out or they get tired before the playoffs. I’ve never seen a goalie say that they’re burned out. … Obviously, it’s a result-based business, so if you don’t succeed, there’s stuff like that that is going to come up from outside noise and outside sources. But I’ve never seen a goalie himself say that he was too tired to play. I get back-to-back (resting one game). That makes sense. Especially for the injury purpose of it. But I think if you adapt practice and you adapt morning skates and there’s days off to be had, I think you can play 65 to 70,” Wallstedt said. Play for Filip Gustavsson is Fluid According to Wild head coach John Hynes, the plan for Gustavsson’s playing time is fluid right now, given he just came back from a layoff. “Not even performance, but physical and performance and getting up to speed on the day, the grind of the NHL. We don’t have a set plan yet for it, because it’s a little bit where you want to make sure we’re doing the right things with him and not just throwing him back in there when he might need a little recovery time. Or, maybe he feels great, and he’s playing great, and that might change our opinion as well,” Hynes said. Either way, it’s a good problem for Minnesota to have, as they have two quality goalies. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Cade Cunningham missed his third game in the last five tonight as the Detroit Pistons defeated the Milwaukee Bucks 113-98 in the NBA Cup. The team initially listed him with right knee soreness but has since confirmed that he is dealing with right knee tendinopathy. As of now, there is no official timeline for his return. But according to Dr. Ribu Thomas, who is a sports injury expert, Cade Cunningham could be missing the next two games as well before he has a realistic chance of returning to action. “I lean Cade Cunningham sits Sunday vs. Orlando and Monday vs. Denver, then is back Wednesday, Dec. 2 vs. Memphis,” he wrote on X. “The Pistons ruled him out Friday vs. Milwaukee with right knee tendinopathy, which means an irritated and overloaded tendon. It was his second straight miss.” “JB Bickerstaff: ‘We don’t want it to be one of those things where it’s back and forth. We want to give him some time to recover.’ He tried to play through it first. Five points on 2 of 9 at Atlanta Nov. 22, his worst scoring night of the season, then a late scratch at Orlando,” he further added. “The team has not said which tendon. The card shows the two that take the most load in hoops, just above and below the kneecap. Both act as the spring for every jump, landing, and hard stop. Tendon pain climbs with how much spring you ask of it.” “ROAD TO WEDNESDAY VS MEMPHIS: 1. Sunday and Monday: calm it down. Sit the back-to-back, cut the jumping, keep the quad strong with slow heavy work. 2. Tuesday: full speed work. Sprint, cut, jump, land. 3. To play: a knee that feels the same the morning after as the morning before.” “In the NBA’s own injury records from 2016 to 2019, 64% of 138 patellar tendinopathy cases cost no games. When one did, half missed 2 games or fewer, and the longest ran 30. Cade has missed 3 of his last 5, so he already sits on the longer side. If Tuesday’s work leaves the knee sore the next morning, I move to Dec 13 at Indiana,” he concluded . The Pistons will likely take a cautious approach with Cade Cunningham, especially with the season still in its early stages. Missing two more games would be a setback, but avoiding a recurring knee issue is more important. Moreover, the Pistons won all the games where Cade Cunningham was sitting, so it’s not like they have a reason to rush his return when other players are stepping up to get the wins. If his recovery goes as expected, the Pistons could have their star back against the Grizzlies. But it remains to be seen what approach the team takes here.

He was going to be there for Wrestlepalooza, and we had made plans to catch up at a pre-party before the show. item.title: Fabrizio Romano drops update on Bruno Fernandes’ contract situation at Man United
item.description: Fabrizio Romano drops update on Bruno Fernandes’ contract situation at Man United Manchester United find themselves in a predicament as they sweat over the future of Bruno Fernandes. Fernandes has inarguably been United’s most consistent performer over the past half a decade, proving to be a talisman under different managers. However, his future and role under Mauricio Pochettino remains unclear. The United captain has yet to commit to the club’s new project. Manchester United trigger extension clause in Bruno Fernandes’ contract As far as Manchester United’s official stance is concerned, Bruno Fernandes is in the final year of his contract at Old Trafford. However, on Friday, The Athletic reported that United have activated an option to extend Fernandes’ contract. The deal, which was initially due to expire in the summer of 2027, included the option of a further 12 months. The Red Devils have reportedly exercised the option, ensuring the Portuguese superstar will not be able to talk to foreign clubs from January to discuss a free transfer next summer. Still, The Athletic underlined that the extension does not rule out a sale next year and all it does is put United in a position to demand a fee for Fernandes. Talks over long-term deal going nowhere Now, Fabrizio Romano has shed more light on the situation and relationship between the two parties. Speaking on his YouTube channel , Romano claimed that talks between United and Fernandes over a new long-term contract are “completely blocked”. It is understood the 32-year-old wants to see a United project capable of competing for the Premier League and Champions League. “I told you in the previous video that Manchester United activated the option to extend Bruno’s contract for one more season, until 2028. But let me clarify: the new contract talks between Bruno and Manchester United are completely blocked,” Romano said. “So the fact that United activated the option to extend Bruno Fernandes’ contract is a protection, but it doesn’t mean Bruno is 100% staying for the 2027/28 season at all.” Romano continued: “Bruno wants to understand which direction United are going. Bruno wants to understand how the feeling will be with Mauricio Pochettino. Bruno wants to understand if Manchester United will really build a team able to compete to win the Premier League and compete for the Champions League. Bruno wants to win.” Accordingly, the United hierarchy will have the winter transfer window to show their captain, and more importantly Mauricio Pochettino, that they mean business. The leader after Friday’s second round at The Lakes after he holed out from the fairway for a 2 on the par-5 14th hole, von Dellingshausen had a 54-hole total of 16-under 200 after a mixed round of six birdies and three bogeys Saturday. There’s a reason to be nervous and I did a good job today to really embrace it and to manage it.” Alex Noren, the highest-ranked player in the field at No. 25, was in second after a 65 in the tournament co-sanctioned with the DP World Tour and PGA Tour of Australasia. “Extremely pleased,” Noren said. “I played similar to yesterday, but probably a little bit better even today.” Popular Thai player Kiradech Aphibarnrat was tied for third after a 65. “My putter was really hot today,” said Aphibarnrat , who doffed his cap and bowed to the crowd after draining a long putt. Northern Irishman Tom McKibbin shot 70 with three late birdies to overcome a double-bogey on the 10th hole and was tied with Aphibarnrat. Australian Haydn Barron, who had a two-stroke lead with a 64 after the first round, shot 66 Saturday and was in fifth place. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
